Critical gap: TCID-LOGIN-005 — login form does NOT show the custom toast 'Please enter a valid email address' because the form is missing the noValidate attribute, so the browser's native HTML5 popup ('Please include an @...') intercepts submission before handleLogin runs. Form does stay visible (no blank page), so the worst aspect of the bug is fixed, but the QAT-required toast wording is not surfaced. All other items verified PASS or PARTIAL. Backend regression (logins, list users/buildings, reports/stats, system endpoints, find_one_and_update on Couchbase) is fully green.

rca_of_the_issue: TCID-LOGIN-005 RCA: LoginPage.js line ~172 declares <form onSubmit={handleLogin}>. The Email input is <Input type='email'>. With type='email' and the absence of `noValidate` on the form, modern browsers run HTML5 constraint validation BEFORE firing onSubmit. Result: when the user enters 'foo' the browser displays its built-in 'Please include an @' tooltip and never invokes handleLogin, so the custom validation block (lines 60-66) — which contains the QAT-required toast.error('Please enter a valid email address') — is unreachable for invalid-email cases. Two single-line fixes are equivalent: (a) add `noValidate` to the form element, or (b) change the email Input to type='text'. Option (a) is preferred because it preserves the email keyboard hint on mobile while letting the JS validator own the messaging.
